title: SpaceXAI Expands Grok Bot Access Across All SuperGrok and Cursor Plans

content_html:
SpaceXAI recently expanded access to Grok Bot. The product was previously available only to SuperGrok Heavy, Cursor Ultra, and Cursor Teams Premium, but now covers the three SuperGrok tiers, Cursor Pro, Pro+, Ultra, and Cursor Teams Standard and Premium. X Premium+ users can link their accounts for access, while Grok and Cursor enterprise customers use it through their organizations.

Pricing is unchanged: Cursor Pro is $20 per month, Pro+ is $60, and Ultra is $200; Teams Standard is $40 per user and Premium is $120. SuperGrok is $30 per month and SuperGrok Plus is $100. X Premium+ is $40 per month in the U.S. and offers a seven-day free trial.

Each Bot runs on a persistent Cursor cloud computer equipped with a browser, file system, and terminal, and tasks continue even after the local device is turned off. The Bot can migrate context and turn one-off actions into scheduled, repeating routines. Use cases include researching sales leads, comparing CRM records, drafting personalized outreach for approval, reproducing product defects, generating customer health reports, and summarizing executive digests from email and calendars.

The limitations are also clear: websites may block automation, present CAPTCHAs, or require login. Such steps are handed off to humans and, when necessary, queued for approval. Early users report that some workflows still require considerable supervision, and the product is still in testing. Paid access is not unlimited; usage resets weekly, and overages can be settled through account-shared on-demand spending. Cursor has not set a fixed task count for the free trial; quotas are measured in agent steps and tokens rather than message count.

This round of expansion is part of an integration path: in April 2026, Cursor formed a compute partnership with SpaceX, using Colossus infrastructure to accelerate model training. On August 14, SpaceX completed its acquisition of Cursor parent company Anysphere, implying an equity valuation of $60 billion, and Grok Bot officially launched the same month. The integration of model capabilities, cloud execution environments, and subscription systems has moved managed agents from a point product to a work platform that can be sold in tiers.
